restatement: Add a Scouting Report linter that Boyd (and Grok Bot, writing a scout) can run before Combine. Given a LintDocument — a ScoutingReport plus an optional checks map from each EARS id to a test or journey ref — it emits a machine-readable LintReport: each rubric criterion → gradeable?/severity/why; each EARS line → check ref or MISSING; each angle pair → Jaccard score and collision flag. Hard findings (ungradeable criterion, missing EARS check, colliding angles, duplicate ids) make ok: false. Soft warnings (weak but pointer-bearing howToGrade) leave ok: true with a non-empty soft list.

return ok: true, summary pass with 1 soft warning, and soft id tests. (Baseline: 0.)

rubric.name: Lint fidelity on fixtures
rubric.howToGrade: Your pooled S1–S8. Then by hand: run lintScoutingReport (or the public core export) on every uploaded JSON fixture and compare with expected.json; run parseMarkdownScout on good-markdown.md. 4 = every fixture matches expectedFor and the three mutations in the oracle (empty howToGrade, identical angles, collide 0.75) each flip ok. One wrong severity on a real fixture = 2 at most. Re-implementing the Jaccard threshold as a different number = 1 at most.

rubric.name: EARS coverage binding
rubric.howToGrade: S3, S9. Confirm CHECK_RE, MISSING on absent keys, and that parseScoutingReport still accepts reports without checks. 4 = missing-ears fixture yields exactly R2,R5,R14,R19,R20 MISSING and good-replay binds all six. Soft-only changes never clear a MISSING.

rubric.name: Angle distinctness
rubric.howToGrade: S4, S8. 4 = collide fixture pair 0-1 scores 0.75 and collide: true; good-replay pairs all score 0; identical-angle mutation hard-fails. A threshold other than 0.45 without a DECISIONS row = 1 at most.

rubric.name: Linter panel screens
rubric.howToGrade: Run cdp-shot.mjs per label on #/picks/<seeded-id>/linter (or the seeded linter route) at 390×844 and 1280×800, light and dark, once on a failing fixture state and once on a passing paste (8 runs), plus the pick page at 390 dark showing the Lint link. 4 = every probe ok: true, scrollWidth ≤ width, every Linter control and link ≥ 44×44 at every width including 1280, and from the 390 dark fail screenshot you can say within 5 seconds that it failed and which EARS are MISSING. 2 = one W7/W8/W9 problem left. 0 = sideways scroll at 390 or a control under 44×44 at 1280. Screenshots required for a 3 or 4.

rubric.name: Untrusted report text safety
rubric.howToGrade: Re-run the safety-fact proof with hostile-markup.json and your own extras: restatement, angle, when, and forbidden carrying markup; an angle carrying javascript:alert(1). Grep src/ui/linter.* for innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval(, new Function, localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie, history., @import, url(http, //fonts.. Any off-origin request, markup from report text, or stored state = 0.

rubric.name: Clean stack, small diff
rubric.howToGrade: git diff --name-only START...<sha> stays inside the touch map; any edit to a do-not-touch file caps this at 1. git diff START -- src/server/http.ts is the static files line plus the POST /api/lint-scout handler (no unrelated churn). git merge-base --is-ancestor START <sha> holds; if dd/p5-replay moved, git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only <sha> origin/dd/p5-replay conflicts at most in docs/DECISIONS.tsv. Compare diff.added + diff.removed with the others (PNG files count as files, not lines). Zero runtime deps.

angles: Rule ledger: start from the three check families; src/core/linter.ts is one registry of rules (gradeability, EARS, angles) checked with satisfies so a new rule fails tsc until its row is complete; one pure lintScoutingReport, thin CLI and POST /api/lint-scout, and a minimal panel that renders the JSON with the binding DOM names; table-driven tests drive every fixture through the harness expectedFor.

Scout checklist: start from the War Room; the Linter panel reads like a scout's clipboard: a big pass/fail chip, three checklists (rubric, EARS, angles) with severity chips, paste-and-Lint on the phone in one thumb-reach stack (safe-area aware); tokens only, both schemes; transitions only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); paused on any 390 px dark screenshot, a stranger can say pass or fail, which EARS are MISSING, and whether angles collide.

Coverage matrix: start from the matrices; EARS×checks as a coverage grid and angles as a pairwise score matrix (cells at least 44x44 on desktop; stacked definition lists on phone); collision and MISSING cells marked aria-invalid / aria-current; VoiceOver order summary, paste, rubric, EARS, angles, hard, soft; extra chrome never breaks the binding DOM or the probe.
forbidden: Draft PRs only. Never mark a PR ready for review, never merge, never enable auto-merge, never deploy or publish anything.
Candidates open no pull request at all (push your branch only). If your environment opens one automatically, it must be a draft with base dd/p5-replay, and say so in your report.
Touch only BoydVC/draft-day. Nothing KPD, kpdlawgroup, or debt-collection related, in code, fixtures, tests or examples.
Do not push to main, dd/scaffold, dd/p1-film-room*, dd/p2-timeline*, dd/p3-lessons*, dd/p4-phone* or dd/p5-replay*, and do not force-push.
Do not edit a file the touch map marks do-not-touch.

No runtime dependencies, no network code (the A15 guard in test/guards.test.ts stays as is), no secrets, no LLM calls, no web fonts or other-origin assets, no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies/history writes.
